clinicalProposition.text: Active acromegaly with chronic GH/IGF-I excess is associated with hypertension through several disease-specific mechanisms, including direct renal sodium and water retention with extracellular-volume expansion and vascular effects. The 2026 acromegaly complications consensus reports that GH acts on distal-nephron epithelial sodium channels, that GH promotes nephron sodium retention and expanded extracellular water, and that biochemical control can lower blood pressure in hypertensive patients. This supports a direct-secondary research pathway when acromegaly activity and blood-pressure chronology are documented; it does not establish that every case of hypertension in a person with acromegaly is attributable to acromegaly.

clinicalProposition.text: Hypertension is a common cardiovascular manifestation of clinically established Cushing's syndrome/hypercortisolism. A European Society of Hypertension endocrine-hypertension consensus describes glucocorticoid excess as the biological basis for the cardiovascular damage of endogenous or exogenous Cushing's syndrome and notes that hypertension may persist even after hormone excess is normalized or steroid therapy is discontinued. This supports a direct-secondary research pathway when the Cushing/hypercortisolism diagnosis and blood-pressure chronology are documented, but other primary and secondary causes of hypertension must still be reviewed.

clinicalProposition.text: Chronic kidney disease is a recognized microvascular complication of longstanding type 1 diabetes, but kidney disease in a person with diabetes is not automatically diabetic kidney disease. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend annual urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio and eGFR assessment after at least 5 years of type 1 diabetes and describe the typical diabetic CKD pattern as longstanding diabetes with albuminuria and/or gradual eGFR loss. This supports a disease-progression research pathway when the diabetes duration, renal phenotype, and chronology fit, while active urine sediment, rapid renal decline, nephrotic syndrome, or other atypical features require investigation for alternative kidney disease.

clinicalProposition.text: Sustained high blood pressure is an established risk factor for kidney disease and can participate in a hypertensive target-organ-damage pathway, but chronic kidney disease is etiologically heterogeneous and can also worsen blood pressure. The 2025 AHA/ACC high-blood-pressure guideline identifies chronic kidney disease among conditions whose development is associated with high blood pressure and addresses hypertension treatment in CKD. Individual review therefore requires renal chronology, albuminuria/eGFR patterns, duration and severity of hypertension, and competing renal causes rather than assuming every CKD diagnosis is caused by hypertension.

clinicalProposition.text: Confirmed male hypogonadism/testosterone deficiency is clinically associated with bone loss and can warrant formal osteoporosis and fracture-risk evaluation. The European Academy of Andrology bone-health guideline states that testosterone deficiency may be clearly associated with bone loss and frailty, recommends complete bone-health assessment and DXA in men with confirmed clinical hypogonadism, and notes that evidence that testosterone replacement prevents fractures is lacking. clinicalProposition.text: Prospective cohort evidence supports a temporal association between migraine and later depression. In a large cohort of women without depression at baseline, active migraine with aura, active migraine without aura, and past migraine were each associated with increased incident depression during long-term follow-up, with higher attack frequency associated with greater risk. The evidence does not establish individual causation, is not proof that depression is secondary to migraine in every patient, and should be interpreted with the individual's psychiatric history, headache burden, treatment, sleep, pain, and other competing contributors.

clinicalProposition.text: Pulmonary hypertension is heterogeneous, so this relationship is limited to a documented pulmonary-vascular or pre-capillary phenotype—especially pulmonary arterial hypertension—in which elevated pulmonary vascular load precedes right-ventricular dysfunction and clinically diagnosed right-sided heart failure. The ESC/ERS pulmonary-hypertension guideline describes symptoms as linked to right-ventricular dysfunction and provides a dedicated advanced right-ventricular-failure pathway for patients with pulmonary hypertension. This mapping does not apply when pulmonary hypertension is secondary to pre-existing left-heart failure (group 2 PH), where the direction of the relationship may be reversed, and it does not establish that every diagnosis coded as congestive heart failure was caused by pulmonary hypertension.
